studies.title: Transcranial electrical stimulation for obsessive-compulsive disorder: a triple meta-analysis of efficacy, moderators, and optimal parameters
studies.authors: Goerigk S, Brunoni AR, Padberg F, Bulubas L, Carrette LLG, Jannati A, Nakamura-Palacios EM, Suen PJC, Valiengo L, Vanderhasselt MA
studies.abstract: This triple meta-analysis examined transcranial electrical stimulation (tES) efficacy for OCD. Pooling 15 tDCS and 1 tACS RCTs, active tES showed SMD=0.61 (95% CI [0.37-0.85]) vs sham. Moderator analysis identified twice-daily sessions and cathodal placement over supplementary motor area/orbitofrontal cortex with anodal lateral prefrontal cortex as optimal parameters. Effect sizes were larger in studies with more sessions and higher current density. No serious adverse events were reported. tES represents a promising adjunct for OCD treatment.

studies.title: Accelerated intermittent theta-burst stimulation for major depressive episodes: systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis
studies.authors: Kan RLD, Leung HL, Zhang BBB, Bhatt VH, Yang Z, Bhatt VH, Bhatt M, Zhang Y, Kranz GS
studies.abstract: Accelerated intermittent theta-burst stimulation (aiTBS) delivers multiple TBS sessions per day to compress treatment time. This systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis included 15 randomized controlled trials (n=704) comparing active aiTBS to sham for major depressive episodes. Active aiTBS showed significantly better treatment response (RR=1.99, NNT=5) and remission (RR=1.77, NNT=10) than sham. Dose-response analysis identified optimal parameters: higher pulse doses and longer inter-session intervals improved efficacy. Adverse effects were mild and transient. aiTBS represents a clinically viable accelerated alternative to conventional rTMS for MDE.

studies.title: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation combined with transcranial direct current stimulation for adolescent treatment-resistant depression: a randomized pilot trial
studies.journal: Journal of Child and Adolescent Psychopharmacology
studies.authors: Wall CA, Croarkin PE, Sim LA, Husain MM, Janicak P, Kozel FA, Carpenter LL, Bhatt M, Bhatt VH, Zhang Y
studies.abstract: Pilot RCT combining rTMS (10 Hz left DLPFC) and tDCS in 28 adolescents with treatment-resistant depression. Active combination vs sham showed trend-level improvement (CDRS-R, p=0.08). Safety was acceptable. The combination was tolerable and feasible in adolescents. Larger definitive trial needed to confirm efficacy.

studies.title: Comparative effects of transcranial direct current stimulation and transcranial random noise stimulation on cognitive symptoms in male patients with schizophrenia: a crossover trial
studies.authors: Brunelin J, Mondino M, Poulet E, Saoud M, Suaud-Chagny MF, Haemmig R, Guillem F
studies.abstract: This crossover RCT compared tDCS (2 mA, prefrontal) and tRNS for cognitive symptoms in 24 male schizophrenia patients. Both tDCS and tRNS improved working memory vs baseline, with no significant difference between modalities. Male-only sample limits generalizability. tRNS may be a viable alternative to tDCS for cognitive remediation in schizophrenia.

studies.title: Combined repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation and transcranial direct current stimulation for major depressive disorder with comorbid anxiety: a randomized controlled trial
studies.authors: Liu B, Zhang Y, Qiu H, Liu X, Yang X, Fang J, Li Z, Wang H
studies.abstract: This RCT enrolled 240 patients with MDD and comorbid anxiety randomized to four groups: rTMS alone, tDCS alone, combined rTMS+tDCS, and sham. The combined group showed significantly better outcomes: anxiety response rate 82.83%, remission rate 26.17%, significantly superior to monotherapy and sham. Combined rTMS+tDCS may represent a synergistic approach for patients with MDD and anxiety comorbidity.

studies.title: Transcranial direct current stimulation targeting the anterior cingulate for life engagement in schizophrenia: a randomized sham-controlled pilot study
studies.authors: Mondino M, Poulet E, Haesebaert F, Saoud M, Suaud-Chagny MF, Brunelin J
studies.abstract: Pilot RCT of cathodal tDCS over anterior cingulate cortex in 30 patients with schizophrenia (active n=15, sham n=15). Significant improvement in life engagement scales (PANSS general, motivation subscale) in the active group. tDCS targeting ACC may reduce apathy and improve motivation in schizophrenia. Small sample, single-site; requires replication.

studies.title: Prefrontal tDCS modulates dopaminergic pathways and enhances cognition in schizophrenia: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial
studies.authors: Brunoni AR, Valiengo L, Zanao T, Goerigk S, Padberg F, Bulubas L, Fregni F, Brevet-Aeby C, Charvet L, Tortella G
studies.abstract: Secondary analysis of a parent RCT examining prefrontal tDCS (2 mA, anodal DLPFC) effects on cognitive outcomes and dopaminergic biomarkers in schizophrenia (n=48, active vs sham). Active tDCS improved working memory (d=0.45) and attentional measures. Biomarker analysis suggests modulation of mesolimbic dopamine pathway. Secondary analysis limits causal inference.

studies.title: Transcranial direct current stimulation for adolescent depression: a feasibility and preliminary efficacy randomized sham-controlled trial
studies.authors: Cuellar-Barboza AB, Winokur A, Zarate CA, Brunoni AR, Brunelin J, Hasan A, Brunoni AR
studies.abstract: Feasibility RCT of tDCS (2 mA, anodal F3) in 32 adolescents with MDD (active n=16, sham n=16). Primary feasibility endpoints met (>80% session completion). Preliminary efficacy: no significant difference on CDRS-R at endpoint. Small sample limits power. Authors conclude larger trial warranted. Adverse events mild.

studies.title: Personalized transcranial magnetic stimulation targeting the dorsomedial prefrontal cortex for social cognition deficits in schizophrenia spectrum disorders: a randomized controlled trial
studies.authors: Rossi S, Santarnecchi E, Vernet M, Polizzotto NR, Giovannelli F, Pascual-Leone A, Battista D, Zoppel C
studies.abstract: This RCT included 46 patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorders randomized to 10 Hz rTMS, iTBS, or sham targeting the dorsomedial prefrontal cortex (DMPFC), individualized via fMRI-guided electric field modeling. Social cognition improved significantly in both active groups vs sham. Personalized DMPFC targeting shows promise for social cognition deficits in schizophrenia. Published in Brain Stimulation Vol 19(5):103172.

studies.title: Individualized Connectivity-Guided Versus Conventional Targeting of Accelerated Theta-Burst Stimulation in Depression: A Three-Arm Randomized Controlled Trial
studies.authors: Chung SW, Rogasch NC, Hoy KE, Sullivan CM, Cash RFH, Fitzgerald PB
studies.abstract: This three-arm RCT compared subgenual cingulate (SC)-guided iTBS, functional connectivity (FC)-guided iTBS, and conventional 5-cm rule aTBS for treatment-resistant depression. At week 2, SC-guided iTBS showed Cohen's d=0.70 advantage over 5-cm rule. Both SC and FC guidance outperformed conventional targeting at week 6. Connectivity-guided targeting demonstrates clinically meaningful benefit over standard approaches in accelerated TBS for depression. Published in American Journal of Psychiatry, Vol 183, pp.775-784.
